question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+6y=3{e}^{5x}.
$$

Select the correct options below.$\,$ An integrating factor for this equation is $I(x)=$ {{field-1}}.

$\,$ The general solution is given by $y(x)=$ {{field-2}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
This equation is already in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)
$$

with $P(x)=6$ and $Q(x)=3{e}^{5x}.$ We proceed to find an integrating factor $I(x)$ using the definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & ={e}^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{\int 6\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{6x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply our differential equation through by $I(x)={e}^{6x}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{6x}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+6y) & ={e}^{6x}\cdot 3{e}^{5x} \\ {e}^{6x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+6{e}^{6x}\cdot y & =3{e}^{11x}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rewrite the left hand side as $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y\cdot I(x))$ and carry out the integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y{e}^{6x}) & =3{e}^{11x} \\ \int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y{e}^{6x})\text{d}x & =\int 3{e}^{11x}\,\text{d}x \\ y{e}^{6x} & =\frac{3{e}^{11x}}{11}+C \\ y & =\frac{3{e}^{5x}}{11}+C{e}^{-6x}\end{aligned}
$$
